text:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Reserved-pool latency spike detected for tenant 'Cobalt' (reserved-pool: rp-cobalt-3). 95th p99 token latency > 3.5s, error rate up to 4%. Auto-page triggered.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident #PD-8421 created and routed to on-call.

jamie_oncall: Acked PD-8421. I'm on it, digging into the reserved pool. @ana_sre can you triage infra side?

ana_sre: on it — looking at node health and queue lengths. Initial glance: I/O stalls on 2/6 GPUs in rp-cobalt-3, backlog of requests piling in the per-tenant queue.

jamie_oncall: Noted. rolling mitigation suggestions: 1) enable burst routing to shared pool, 2) scale up reserved pool (manual add), 3) flip to fallback model (cobalt-v1.3-q8) for latency-sensitive routes. Which do we want first?

tim_runtime: quick check: kv-cache hit rates for Cobalt are fine (~88%). This looks like tail latency from a single worker node. If we kick it, requests should drain to other nodes. I can trigger a graceful drain on node rp-cobalt-3-node-22. Command: `infra pool drain rp-cobalt-3-node-22 --grace 30s`

ana_sre: go ahead, tim — I'll watch eviction metrics.

jamie_oncall: executing drain now.

ops_lead_lee: FYI, customer success says one Cobalt tenant app reported timeouts in prod (support ticket #C-4944). Maya, do you have details?

maya_cs: confirmed — Cobalt ops noticed ~12% client-side timeouts, mostly on their interactive chat endpoint. They flagged increased latency starting ~09:11 UTC. They asked for ETA. I'll message them with we are investigating and will follow up within 15m.

(10s later)

incident-bot: Action taken: rp-cobalt-3-node-22 marked draining by jamie_oncall. Autoscaler not triggered due to reserved capacity floor.

ana_sre: Seeing some requests failover to rp-cobalt-3-node-23 but tail latency still high. Node-22 shows GPU watchdog restarts in syslog — CUDA driver warnings around 09:10. Copying a small log snippet:
```
[09:10:12] GpuWatchdog: gpu0: context lost, driver timeout.
[09:10:13] Restarting runtime process on gpu0
[09:10:13] RequestQueue: 240 reqs dropped on gpu0
```

jamie_oncall: That explains the 4% error increase. Two options: reprovision node (replacement) or route traffic away and autoscale burst capacity. Which is faster?

tim_runtime: Replacement takes ~7-10m to provision new GPU node in this region. Burst routing to shared pool is immediate if policy allows; need to lift tenant burst throttle. I can trigger burst-routing override for Cobalt for 15m: `route override set --tenant cobalt --to shared-burst --ttl 15m`

jamie_oncall: Do it. Also flip critical endpoints to fallback model now: `deploy-route --tenant cobalt --route /chat --model cobalt-v1.3-q8 --priority high`

tim_runtime: route override applied. fallback model deployed to the route.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-8421 acknowledged by jamie_oncall at 09:12:10 UTC.

maya_cs: I updated the customer with that we're routing to fallback and working on node replacement; told them we'll follow up with a post-incident note. They replied: "Thanks — please keep us posted, this is impacting a small % of users."

ana_sre: Reprovision started for rp-cobalt-3-node-22 replacement. Provision ID: prov-8812. ETA ~9m. Monitoring IO and node join events.

ops_lead_lee: Can we adjust request retries client-side for them? If we add a soft 250ms retry they'd see fewer visible errors. Maya can you coordinate?

maya_cs: Pushed a recommendation in their ticket: enable 1 retry with 200ms jitter for now. They acknowledged.

(3m)

ana_sre: New node provisioning completed and joined cluster. Healthchecks passing. Starting warmup (model cache preload).

tim_runtime: Warmup done. Removing route override now so traffic will start rebalancing back to reserved pool. Command: `route override delete --tenant cobalt --to shared-burst`

jamie_oncall: Monitoring 95th and error rate. 95th latency back down to 420ms, errors <0.5%. Marking incident as mitigated.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-8421 updated to status: resolved (mitigated) by jamie_oncall at 09:21:15 UTC.

maya_cs: Customer updated with resolution and root-cause statement pending. They want a short postmortem.

ana_sre: Root cause: GPU driver timeout on rp-cobalt-3-node-22 caused runtime restarts and request drops; cluster didn't autoscale because reserved-capacity floor prevented automatic burst. Action items: 1) tune burst policy for critical tenants, 2) add GPU health watchdog alerts earlier (pre-timeout), 3) improve automatic re-route to fallback models.

ops_lead_lee: I'll own the policy change and follow up with a PR for config. Assigning to ops_lead_lee.

jamie_oncall: Handoff: I'm going offline for lunch in ~10m; @ana_sre will be primary for follow-ups. Ana, please monitor for 30m and cut a short postmortem draft.

ana_sre: Acknowledged — will monitor and draft postmortem.

incident-bot: Note: channel set to incident-review and postmortem checklist reminder queued for 1h.

(End of thread)
